final_message:
I built the Ploverdesk landing page as a React + Vite page with plain CSS. It has not been built or opened in a browser: the sandbox refused to run `node` and `npm` ("operation not permitted"), so `npm run build` never ran here and the TypeScript is unchecked.

The page is built around one picture: an example invoice checked line by line against its purchase order and delivery note. Lines that match get a small grey tick. The three that don't (a wrong quantity, a wrong unit price, a delivery that never arrived) are circled in red and named in words. On load the ticks and circles draw in once, row by row, in under a second. With reduced motion turned on they are simply there.

**Decision you should know about:** that example uses made-up quantities and prices (120 × 4.20 and so on). The founders said "invent no other figure". I read that as no claims about the company, so I kept the example and labelled it on the page as illustrative values. If they meant it literally, those numbers should be replaced or the example removed.

**What's on the page**
- **Top of the page:** the headline "Only the invoice lines that don't match reach your desk.", one paragraph, the "Start the 14-day trial" button (/trial), a quieter "Book a demo" link (/demo), and the terms (no card, 290 EUR per month per company, no limit on users). The example invoice sits beside this on wide screens and below it on narrow ones. Below 720px the invoice table becomes one block per line, each figure next to its label.
- **"How an invoice travels":** arrives by email, checked three ways, then either straight to payment approval or the mismatched line goes to a person, then exported as CSV or through the API.
- **"Price and terms":** price, users, trial, export, Frankfurt hosting, and founded 2025 with six people in Rotterdam, followed by the same two actions.
- **Style:** white page, near-black text and buttons, red used only for "this line needs a person". Square corners, no shadows, the system font. No web font was loaded, since none was approved and there is no network.

**Files:** `index.html`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/index.css`, the new `src/tokens.css` (all colours, sizes and timings), `MASTER.md` (the design rules), and two throwaway previews, `preview/thesis.html` and `preview/design-system.html`.

**Process:** nobody could approve anything, so the design direction and design rules in `MASTER.md` are marked **UNVALIDATED**. They were decided from the brief alone.

**Checked here**
- **Contrast**, computed from the colour values: body text 17.8:1, secondary text 8.4:1, labels 5.8:1 on white, red 6.5:1 on white and 5.8:1 on its pale row background, button hover 11.7:1. The thin rule under the table header is 2.95:1 on the grey table background; it is decoration, not a control.
- **Audit script:** 28 checks ran and one came back with a finding: hover rules with no transition. That one is a false alarm, because the transition sits on the base rule (`src/index.css:77` and `:98`). The 18 checks for generic AI-page habits found nothing.
- **Read by hand:**
  - The page uses a real table rather than a fake screenshot.
  - There is one rule under the table header and no rule on every row, no monospace, no testimonials, no logos and no usage numbers.
  - The founding year and every other company fact come from the brief.
  - The top of the page and "Price and terms" share the same left/right split, but they hold different content.
- **Accessibility:**
  - Every colour value lives in `src/tokens.css`.
  - The reduced-motion rule is at `src/index.css:509`.
  - Links and buttons show a focus outline (`:61`) and have hover, pressed and disabled styles.
  - Nothing animates position or size.
  - The tick and circle graphics are hidden from screen readers; the result is also given in words.
  - Nothing appears or disappears, so there are no exit animations to check.

**Not verified here, for you to run**
- `npm run build` (it also runs `tsc --noEmit`).
- The page at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px wide: no sideways scrolling and nothing clipped. The tightest spot is the invoice table at 1024px, where line names and results are allowed to wrap.
- Whether the headline, actions and whole invoice fit before any scrolling on a 1280×720 screen. I estimated about 700px, but didn't measure it.
- A Chrome DevTools Performance recording of the load: no frame over 16.7ms.
- The page with the operating system's "reduce motion" setting on: the ticks and circles should appear with no draw-in.

**Other notes**
- No dependency was installed, and no animation library was needed.
- bunshin (genjutsu's pipeline for whole multi-page sites) would not have fit a single page, so I didn't propose it.

Modules loaded: tells (with its web reference), motion-principles, css-native, mobile-principles, design-audit. I ran ui-ux-pro-max's design lookup script but did not read the module itself.
Modules not loaded: none

How did it come out? One minute, and plain or wrong counts as much as good:
